title: What Happens When an AI Agent Uses a Tool?
note: M2 dry run (no render). Scenes are anchored to narration words, never to guessed seconds. Times in the estimated storyboard are words / 2.5 per second.

brief.audience: General technology learners; no programming knowledge assumed
brief.takeaway: An AI agent does not run tools itself: the model writes a request, the app carries it out, and the result goes back to the model.
brief.tone: clear, friendly, a little surprising; never hype

scenes.title: Hook
scenes.visual: Calm plain background. The line 'An AI chat model only writes text.' is already on screen at frame 0 and holds. At 'So how does' a second line, 'So how does an agent act?', fades in beneath it.
scenes.transition: Cold open on the text, no intro animation. Exit: cross-dissolve into the diagram.
scenes.caption_note: Hook text is the caption; word-synced captions are hidden in this scene.

direction.takeaway: An AI model only writes text; something else must do the real work.
direction.why: A held statement lets the contradiction land (a model that only writes text, yet agents act); one cue-timed second line adds the question without competing with it. A diagram here would explain before the viewer cares.

motion.primary: second line fades in once, on its spoken cue

reframe.16:9: Two headline lines left-aligned in the middle third, generous empty space to the right.
reframe.9:16: The same two lines stacked in the upper-middle; the lower caption band stays empty.

verify: 'Only writes text' is true of a text chat model; some models also produce images or audio, which is why the wording says 'AI chat model'.

scenes.title: The tool menu
scenes.visual: Static concept diagram. Left: a MODEL box. Right: an APP box. Between them a card titled TOOLS lists three generic tools, each with a name and a one-line description (Weather: looks up the weather. Email: sends a message. Files: opens a file). Rounded shapes, warm palette, no brand marks.
scenes.transition: Cross-dissolve in from the hook text. The whole diagram is present from the start of the scene and holds.
scenes.caption_note: Word-synced captions in the bottom band; menu text is at least as large as the captions so it can be read at a glance.

direction.takeaway: The app gives the model a menu of tools, each with a name and description.
direction.why: The director preferred a hand-drawn look to feel friendly to non-technical learners, but p5.brush is a candidate awaiting owner review, so the scene uses the native SVG treatment with rounded shapes and a warm palette. No motion: the viewer needs to read three names and descriptions. If p5.brush is later promoted, this is the first scene to retry.

motion.primary: none: held concept diagram (MODEL, APP, three-item TOOLS card)

direction.exit: cross-dissolve; the stage persists into the next scene
direction.text_zone: diagram inside the title-safe box; labels never under the caption band

reframe.16:9: MODEL left, APP right, TOOLS card centred between and above them.
reframe.9:16: MODEL on top, TOOLS card in the middle, APP below; the same relationships read top to bottom.

verify: 'The app gives the model a menu of tools with names and descriptions' was checked against Anthropic's tool-use overview (the model decides based on the request and each tool's description); wording in other providers' docs is unchecked.

scenes.title: The model asks
scenes.starts_at: ask do i need a jacket
scenes.visual: Same stage. The TOOLS card dims. A small question chip 'Do I need a jacket in Austin?' sits at the MODEL. At 'It writes out a request' a short request card appears beside the MODEL: 'use: Weather / place: Austin'. Nothing else moves; the APP box stays quiet.
scenes.transition: Same stage continues; the TOOLS card dims by cross-fade at the scene start.
scenes.caption_note: Word-synced captions in the bottom band; the request card text is at least caption size.

direction.takeaway: The model does not run the tool; it writes out a request for it.
direction.why: One card appearing on the words 'writes out a request' ties the idea to its sound; moving anything else would split attention from the single new object.

motion.primary: request card appears once, on its spoken cue; everything else holds

cues.do: request card appears beside the MODEL

direction.exit: request card stays; connectors draw in the next scene
direction.text_zone: request card inside the title-safe box, clear of the caption band

reframe.16:9: Request card to the right of the MODEL, pointing toward the APP.
reframe.9:16: Request card directly below the MODEL, above the APP.

verify: The real request is a structured block (a tool name plus its inputs), not a sentence; the on-screen card must stay a short labelled card and the narration says 'writes out a request', not 'plain English'.

scenes.title: The app does the work
scenes.visual: Same stage, a SERVICE box appears at the far end (weather service). On 'reads that request' a line draws from the request card to the APP. On 'asks a weather service' a line draws from the APP to the SERVICE. On 'gets an answer' a return line draws from the SERVICE back to the APP.
scenes.transition: A SERVICE box is present at scene start (cross-fade); connectors draw on their cues.
scenes.caption_note: Word-synced captions in the bottom band; box labels at least caption size.

direction.takeaway: The app carries out the request and gets the real answer from a service.
direction.why: The order of hand-offs is the lesson, so each connector draws exactly when its step is spoken; a static diagram would hide the sequence. Each draw is one segment on its own cue, not the rule's overlapping stagger, so narration controls the timing.

motion.primary: three connector lines draw on, one per spoken step

cues.do: line draws from the request card to the APP
line draws from the APP to the SERVICE
return line draws from the SERVICE to the APP

direction.exit: lines stay drawn; the next scene continues the return path
direction.text_zone: diagram inside the title-safe box, clear of the caption band

reframe.16:9: Flow runs left to right: request card, APP, SERVICE; the return line curves back under the outbound line.
reframe.9:16: Flow runs top to bottom with the return line on the right side; labels stay on the left.

verify: 'The app does the real work' holds for client tools. Provider-hosted server tools (for example web search or code execution) run on the provider's side, so decide whether a short on-screen note or narration caveat is wanted for accuracy.

scenes.title: The answer goes back
scenes.starts_at: the app hands that answer back
scenes.visual: A line draws from the APP back to the MODEL (mirroring the outbound path, because coming back is the idea). An answer card labelled 'example data: 12 degrees, cold' appears at the MODEL. At 'take a jacket' a reply card 'Yes, take a jacket.' appears under it.
scenes.transition: Continues the same stage; no scene-level transition effect.
scenes.caption_note: Word-synced captions in the bottom band; 'example data' label is always visible on the answer card.

direction.takeaway: The answer goes back to the model as another message, so it can finish its reply.
direction.focal: the answer card, then the reply card
direction.why: The return line mirrors the outbound path because 'coming back' is the point; the two cards each appear on their own words so the viewer sees answer first, reply second.

motion.primary: return line draws to the MODEL on its cue; answer card then reply card appear on theirs

cues.do: return line draws from the APP to the MODEL and the answer card appears
reply card appears under the answer card

direction.text_zone: cards inside the title-safe box, clear of the caption band

reframe.16:9: Return line runs right to left under the outbound lines; answer and reply cards stack beside the MODEL.
reframe.9:16: Return line runs bottom to top on the left side; answer and reply cards stack under the MODEL.

verify: The weather values on screen are illustrative and must stay labelled 'example data'.
'The result goes back as another message' matches Anthropic's tool-use overview (a follow-up message carrying a result tied to the original request).

scenes.title: The loop
scenes.visual: The stage clears to a three-step loop diagram: MODEL ASKS, APP ACTS, MODEL READS, joined by arrows. Each arrow draws on its spoken step; labels do not move once shown. The final arrow closes the loop.
scenes.transition: Cross-dissolve from the example stage to the loop diagram.
scenes.caption_note: Word-synced captions in the bottom band; step labels are at least caption size.

direction.takeaway: An agent loops: the model asks, the app acts, the model reads the result.
direction.why: A recap must be rememberable: three labels that stay put, with arrows that draw on the three spoken verbs, give the viewer the loop as a shape they can repeat.

motion.primary: three loop arrows draw on their spoken steps; labels stay still

cues.do: first arrow draws into MODEL ASKS
second arrow draws into APP ACTS
third arrow draws and closes the loop

direction.text_zone: diagram inside the title-safe box, clear of the caption band

reframe.16:9: Three steps in a row with a return arrow underneath closing the loop.
reframe.9:16: Three steps stacked top to bottom with the return arrow along the right edge.

verify: 'Sometimes it repeats before the final answer': the tool-use overview shows one round trip and defers loop mechanics to a separate page, so confirm that page before keeping the claim.

scenes.title: Next
scenes.visual: Static end card with one line: 'Next: what happens when a tool call goes wrong?'.
scenes.transition: Cross-dissolve from the loop. The card holds to the last frame.
scenes.caption_note: The end-card line is the caption; word-synced captions hidden in this scene.

direction.takeaway: Next question: what happens when a tool call goes wrong?
direction.why: A held card gives the question room; any motion would only delay the end.

reframe.16:9: One line centred, large, with empty space around it.
reframe.9:16: The same line centred in the upper-middle, clear of the lower caption band.
